newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian population growth falls under 2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Algerian population growth falls under 2 pct.

text.p: Algeria's population growth fell to less than two percent this year for the first time since the country's independence 34 years ago, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Thursday.

But the Algerian National Statistics Office head Mohamed Berkani said the fall was not enough. The population was still growing by more than 500,000 people a year, compounding the country's social crisis.

"Obviously, the population growth is better than the 3.4 percent rate increase seen in the 1960s. But it is still too much because the current growth means another 520,000 more people (each year)," said Berkani quoting by APS.
Algeria's population will reach 28.9 million in 1997 from 28.3 million now, adding to the potentially-rich country's problems of overcrowding and 2.1 million unemployed.
